layers.label: Business
layers.description: Product: what the feature is for, the user story, decisions and sign-off.

kinds.label: User Story
kinds.description: Who the user is, what they do, acceptance criteria. Approved by product, verified by QA.

layers.label: Frontend
layers.description: The client team: what it asks of the backend and what it shipped.

kinds.label: Frontend Requirements
kinds.description: What the client needs from the backend to build the story: data, endpoints, errors, behaviour.

kinds.label: Frontend Delivery
kinds.description: What the client shipped: screens, state, calls made, what is left.

layers.label: Backend
layers.description: The API team: what it shipped and how the client calls it.

kinds.label: Backend Delivery
kinds.description: What the backend shipped: endpoints, tables, how it works, what exists, gaps.

kinds.label: Backend Integration
kinds.description: How the client calls what was shipped: screens to calls, flows, shapes, errors, rules. `current` hands it off (the frontend and QA use it); it is done, Delivered, only when the build computes it: QA Backend passing and the Frontend Delivery done in its scope, nothing pending.

layers.label: QA
layers.description: Expected behaviour as artefacts (tables, diagrams), not test code; one note per side.

kinds.label: QA Backend
kinds.description: Expected API behaviour: given / when / then, state diagram, error matrix, verdict.

kinds.label: QA Frontend
kinds.description: Expected screen behaviour against the story: states, journeys, error copy, verdict.

cardCodes.description: Every card (one Markdown file in the tree) carries one unique code: <prefix>-<number>. A task's, a bug's and a decision's code is its id (T-004, B-01, D-04); every other card gets the next free number for its kind's prefix, kept in tree/cards.json and listed in Card Index.md; a code is never reused. A bug is its own note type, type: bug (tags bug, bug/<status>): it takes the task statuses and sits on the Task Board and the Backlog with the tasks, has its own B prefix and number sequence, and hangs under the task it was found against (parent) or the card named in foundOn, never under the feature's story. It is created with node scripts/build-tree.mjs --scaffold bug from templates/Bug Template.md, and its file lives in bugs/<Title>.md whatever it hangs under: a bug and a needs-decision card are named by their title, the code in id: and aliases: (aliases: [B-01]) and in Card Index.md.

taskFlow.description: The card flow a task draws under itself: the same chain a feature draws, at task scope, tied to the task's own story. `kinds` are the slots; a slot with no note yet is a dashed placeholder blocked by the card before it, exactly as at feature level. `tasks` says which tasks draw it: a list of task ids turns it on for those only, which is how a change to the flow is tried on one ticket before the vault takes it; "all" turns it on for every task. A task whose feature is frontendOnly skips the kinds in frontendOnly.skips.

priorities.description: The priority enum every card may carry (priority: <id> in frontmatter, mirrored by the tag priority/<id>). A layer note without one inherits its task's or feature's; a sub-task its parent's. The tree draws it as a flag in the level's colour. aliases are the old P-codes, accepted with a warning.

levels.label: Critical
levels.description: Launch blocker: nothing ships without it.

levels.label: High
levels.description: Needed for the release; scheduled next.

levels.label: Low
levels.description: Nice to have; whenever there is room.

resolutions.description: How a bug ended, typed as resolution: <id> on a bug card only (type: bug) and mirrored by the tag resolution/<id>. It never replaces status:, which says where the card stands (todo … done) and nothing about the outcome; a bug closed with status: done and a pending list is still Partial, whatever its resolution says. The build errors on the key anywhere but a bug and warns when a bug is done without one. Set by the agents in agents.reservedFields.resolution (the PM, who closes bugs, and QA, who files them); the rule is project/Agent Rules.md §4.

levels.label: Fixed
levels.description: The behaviour changed: code shipped and the bug is gone.

levels.label: By design
levels.description: The build was right and the expectation was wrong; the words moved instead. The decision card it rests on is named in the card's related.

levels.label: Duplicate
levels.description: Another card covers it, named in related.

levels.label: Cannot reproduce
levels.description: Not seen again on a named build.

levels.label: Won't fix
levels.description: Real, accepted and not scheduled; the gap stays written down, with the decision card it rests on in related.

deadlines.description: deadline: YYYY-MM-DD on any card (a layer note inherits its task's or feature's). The tree colours a clock by how much of the last windowDays is left, split evenly over zones from farthest to nearest: with windowDays 3, more than two days left is on track (green), the day before is due soon (yellow), the deadline day is the last day (red); after it the card is missed (skull). The colour is computed when the page is viewed, never written into the generated files.

stages.description: Where the product is in its life, typed by the owner as stage: <id> in business/Project Overview.md and drawn as a chip on the project card beside its computed status. A stage is never computed; exit is the test that moves it to the next one. requiresRelease names a release target whose features must all be Done before the stage is typed: the build warns when they are not.

levels.label: Prototype
levels.description: Parts are built; the main flow does not run end to end yet.
levels.exit: One user can complete the main flow.

levels.label: MVP
levels.description: Building the smallest set of features you would release (the features with release: mvp).
levels.exit: Every mvp feature is Done and its QA passes.

levels.label: Beta
levels.exit: The release decision is taken on a decision card.

levels.label: Live
levels.exit: The product is being phased out.

releases.description: The release a feature is scoped to: release: <id> on the feature card, mirrored by the tag release/<id>; its layer notes and tasks inherit it. The project card counts, per target, the features Done out of the total. A feature without one shows as No release.

targets.label: MVP
targets.description: In the first release: nothing ships without it.

targets.label: Later
targets.description: Not scheduled for a release yet.

environments.description: Where a delivery runs: deployedTo: [<id>, …] on the kinds listed, empty until the layer deploys it. Environments are not stages: the project can be at mvp and run on all three.

branches.description: Vault branches, for every agent: <prefix>/<agent>/<M-NN>-<module-id>/<F-NN>-<feature-id>/<card>-<what-you-do>, printed by node scripts/build-tree.mjs --branch <agent> <card> [<what>]. The prefix is tickets for the cards that ask for or plan work (the kinds listed under tickets), docs for the archive of what is (every other card, the rules and the reference notes). Code repositories keep <module>/<T-NNN>/<what-you-do> (project/Workflow.md §2).

projectAreas.label: Business docs
projectAreas.description: The product, glossary, feature map, status reports.

projectAreas.label: Frontend docs
projectAreas.description: The client contract, API guide, migrations the client must make, the frontend agent prompt.

projectAreas.description: The workflow, the agent rules and the docs tree: rules every layer follows.

agents.description: The agents that edit this vault, one per role, invoked as /<id> in Claude Code (.claude/skills/<id>/SKILL.md loads the note). Each one writes only what its `writes` block names: `types` (structural note types; `bug` is a bug card, type: bug),`kinds` (layer-note kinds, feature- and task-level), `taskLabels` (task notes carrying one of these labels), `paths` (globs; `except` removes); `editOnly` is the same but Edit only, never a rewrite or a new file. `signs` are the kinds where the agent may change only the sign-off lines (status, approvedBy / approvedAt, decidedBy / decidedAt, updated, tags, the H1); `fields` the frontmatter keys it may set on any card. Every agent raises the decision card its own card needs (`decision` in its `types`), but only an agent with `decision` in `signs` may set a decision's status, decidedBy or decidedAt, and only such an agent writes the decision record that takes it (`decision-record` in its `types`): the answer lives on that card, DR-NN for D-NN, never in the decision card (project/Agent Rules.md §4). Every agent may add a flag line (> ⚠ Affected by …) under any note's H1; nobody edits a generated file or design/Wireframe Brief.md. One entry may set `writes.all: true` instead (the admin, /admin): the guard then refuses it nothing, generated files and the brief included; it is the user's own hand for repairs, not a role. While no agent is active every write is refused and the agent asks which one to use. The hook in .claude/settings.json runs scripts/agent-guard.mjs to enforce this; the shared protocol is project/Agent Protocol.md.

reservedFields.description: Frontmatter keys only the agents listed may add, change or remove, on any note, whoever owns the note otherwise (the admin excepted): a feature's release and the project's stage are the owner's, a bug's resolution is the PM's and QA's (project/Agent Rules.md §4).
